sections.html:
Newberry County lies in central South Carolina, and the city of Newberry is both the seat and the biggest community. Households numbered 15,039 in 2020, with 37,719 residents, and the 2025 estimate stands at 39,561. Roughly 30,400 parcels are on the books, manufactured homes among them, and most deals are local.

Land inside the Belfast Wildlife Management Area and the Sumter National Forest is off the market, so not every acre can be bought or built on. Mill-era houses along farm roads are common, often with their original wiring, plumbing and roofs, which is exactly where buyers' lenders push back.

Because work clusters around a few plants, one layoff or relocation can force a quick sale by a household that is already behind on tax and mortgage payments.

sections.h2: Which Newberry County offices handle property tax
sections.html:
The Assessor and the Delinquent Tax Collector share one address: 1512 Martin Street, Newberry, SC 29108. County administration is at 1309 College Street.

OfficePhone and hours
Assessor803-321-2125, option 1; assessorsoffice@newberrycounty.gov; 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. weekdays
Delinquent Tax Collector(803) 321-2128; 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. weekdays
County administration803-321-2100; 1309 College Street

Ownership, valuation and assessment records for every piece of real property live with the Assessor. Request forms there for legal residence, a new mailing address, agricultural use or a Notice of Objection.

sections.h2: Penalties on a Newberry County tax bill
sections.html:
State law, S.C. Code 12-45-180, sets the late charges here. Expect 3 percent from January 16, 7 percent more on February 2 and 5 percent more on March 17, the day the Treasurer may add a tax execution. Compare these dates with your own bill.

Overdue accounts are pursued through all legal avenues by the Delinquent Tax Office, which files bankruptcy claims in federal court and claims with the Probate Court. Heirs should know that a claim may already be waiting in probate when an estate owes tax.

American Financial Credit Services handles some personal property accounts. After an account goes to that firm, the county will not accept payment until the firm is paid, and its fee is added.

Delinquent properties go on the block once a year at Piedmont Technical College's Newberry campus, 1922 Wilson Road. Bidders register shortly before the sale, or earlier in person at 1512 Martin Street or by email with a photo ID copy.

  • The Newberry Observer carries the property notices for three straight weeks ahead of the sale.
  • Mobile homes go into the same sale.
  • Date and time change yearly, so ask the Delinquent Tax Collector.

S.C. Code 12-51-90 gives the former owner twelve months to redeem. Interest runs 3 percent of the bid for the first quarter, then 6, 9 and 12 in later quarters. Without a redemption, the buyer gets a deed. An owner who spots a sale coming can list the house first and let the title company pay the county at closing.

Your tool is the Notice of Objection, filed with the Assessor within 90 days of the day the assessment notice was mailed. The mailing date printed on your own notice starts that count.

You may object to fair market value, special use value or the assessment ratio. Someone who never got a notice can appeal in writing at any time. A filing made ahead of the first penalty date affects this year's bill, and a later one affects next year's.

sections.h2: Legal residence and the 4 percent ratio
sections.html:
A new owner who will live in the house should apply early for legal residence status. Four percent is the ratio for an occupied home rented no more than 72 days a year, and the filing deadline is the first penalty date.

Skip it and 6 percent applies for that year, inflating the tax part of the buyer's mortgage payment. Mentioning the form during the sale helps the buyer avoid that.

Tracts used commercially for crops or timber can qualify for agricultural use valuation. When part of your land carries that status, find out from the Assessor how a sale or a change of use affects the value before signing.

sections.h2: What a Newberry County seller should do first
sections.html:
Begin by learning what is owed and which office holds the record. A short call now can save weeks.

  • Assessor, 803-321-2125, option 1: confirm the owner of record, the mailing address and whether a legal residence form is on file.
  • Delinquent Tax Collector, (803) 321-2128: if any year is past due, request a payoff that holds through your likely closing date.
  • After an owner's death, ask whether a claim has gone to the Probate Court.
  • Look in The Newberry Observer for a tax sale notice.

Owing tax will not stop you from selling. At closing the county is paid from your proceeds, so get a current payoff before that day, in writing if you can.

Hand the title company the payoff, the parcel details and your target closing date early. When closing slides, request a fresh payoff, because penalties from January 16, February 2 or March 17 change the number.

A cash sale avoids the lender appraisal, repair demands from a buyer and the wait for mortgage approval. With an old mill-era house or an estate carrying a probate claim, the shorter path can outweigh a somewhat higher listing price.

sections.h2: Timeline for a Newberry County sale
sections.html:
Plan around three dates on the tax calendar: January 16, February 2 and March 17. A sale that closes before January 16 pays the base balance only. One that closes later pays more at each step, and after March 17 the account can head toward execution and the annual sale.

Order matters. Pull the payoff, list the house or accept a cash offer, order the title work and schedule the closing. Each piece takes time, so a seller already past a penalty date should start with the payoff call and not wait for a buyer to appear.

Houses that pass through an estate often carry the oldest tax problems. Because the Delinquent Tax Office files claims with the Probate Court, an executor should ask early whether one exists and for what years. Settle the figure before listing so the sale price and the payoff can be compared honestly.

Family members who live far away can start by phone. The Assessor can confirm who is the owner of record and where bills are being mailed, and a wrong mailing address is a common reason an owner never sees a bill. Use the mailing address change form to fix it.

Once the owner of record, the mailing address and the payoff are clear, the title company can take over the paperwork and pay the county at closing.

sections.h2: What to bring to the office
sections.html: Photo ID and the property address are the basics for a trip to 1512 Martin Street. Executors should add proof that they may act for the owner. Phone ahead, since the Assessor and the Delinquent Tax Collector keep different records under one roof.

faqs.q: Where is the Newberry County Assessor's office?
faqs.a: 1512 Martin Street, Newberry, SC 29108. Call 803-321-2125, option 1. The office is open 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays.

faqs.q: Who collects delinquent taxes in Newberry County?
faqs.a: The Delinquent Tax Collector, at 1512 Martin Street. The number is (803) 321-2128.

faqs.q: When is the Newberry County tax sale?
faqs.a: Once a year, at Piedmont Technical College's Newberry campus. Ask the Delinquent Tax Collector for the date and registration time.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Newberry County assessment?
faqs.a: Submit a written Notice of Objection to the Assessor within 90 days after the notice is mailed.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Newberry County house that owes taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, the county is paid out of your proceeds at closing. Request a payoff first.
